body:
You are drafting short lines for the Narrator of a single-player D&D 5e computer game built on the Curse of Strahd adventure (Barovia, gothic horror). Answer in plain text only. Do not send messages to anyone else and finish in this one reply.

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller who has watched a great many adventurers walk into Barovia and very few walk out. Not the party's enemy and not its friend; fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather: with interest, without illusions. Rules we hold every Narrator line to:

1. Second person, present tense ("You step inside"). Never "the party", never past tense.
2. Dry, ominous, never cruel. The world is cruel; the Narrator isn't. It never gloats and never cheers.
3. Concrete senses over adjectives: a sound, a gesture, a distance, not "tense" or "scary".
4. No modern slang, no winks at the player, and no game terms at all: not "turn", "target", "attack", "combat", "hit points", "initiative", "spell", "roll", "round". Say what happens in the world.
5. Combat lines are fast: ONE sentence, under 15 words. (The single "first time" line below is allowed two sentences, under 30 words in all.)
6. Do not use the character-name placeholders {name} or {target}. Lines are recorded by an actor, so write Ireena's name out when you need it.

## What is changing in play (this is the thing the lines have to carry)

Ireena Kolyana travels with the party as a companion (a "guest"). Until now she fought like a party member and, being a minor noble with about nine hit points, died easily, which made players leave her behind. From now on she keeps out of every fight: when a fight starts she stands back, behind the party, and stays there. She takes no turns. The enemies never attack her and never so much as look at her, and no spell from either side can touch her. The player does not control her and cannot put her in harm's way.

The fiction we want the Narrator to hint at, once, without explaining it: something in this valley has been told whose she is, and goes round her the way water goes round a stone. (Strahd, the vampire lord, has claimed her; she is the woman he has hunted across centuries. The party and the player do NOT know that yet. Never write the name Strahd, never write "vampire", never say who or what claims her; leave it ominous and unexplained.)

Ireena hates being kept back. She is not a damsel and tells anyone who treats her like one that she is not made of glass. She is tall, red-haired, in her early twenties, proud, direct and dry, and she keeps a sword by the fire and knows how to use it. The Narrator is fond of her and doesn't pity her. Her grief shows as precision, her fear as a straight back.

Existing Narrator lines about her, so you can match the register:
- "Ireena sits with her knees drawn up and a blanket round her shoulders, watching the dark. She doesn't sleep much. You understand why."
- "Ireena is sharpening a knife she doesn't need, because her hands want something to do."
- "Ireena slows at the crossroads and reads every arm of the signpost twice, as if it might have changed its mind about where things are."
- "Heads turn as Ireena comes into the firelight, and the music falters for half a bar. Then the fiddler plays louder, as if to make up for it."
- "Ireena looks at the doll on the offering stone for a long time, and doesn't touch it."
- "People turn to look at Ireena as she passes, and then look quickly away, as if her red hair were a lamp left burning after curfew."

Existing fight lines, for the register of fast combat lines:
- "The blow lands like a verdict."
- "Steel answers steel, and steel wins."

## What I need

A. The FIRST-TIME line, played once ever, as the first fight begins with Ireena along. Give 3 different options. Two sentences at most, under 30 words in all. It must make plain that she stands apart from the fight and that the enemies do not turn on her, and carry the hint above without naming it.

B. Eight candidate lines for the REGULAR line, one of which is shown as each later fight begins (the game never repeats one until all have been shown). Each is ONE sentence, under 15 words, and each uses a different image, for example where she stands, what her hands do, the enemies' eyes sliding past her, the distance between her and the blow, her jaw, her sword hilt, the thing she would say and doesn't. Rules for B: she does not draw steel or swing it; she is never hurt or threatened; no line may suggest the party is guarding her; none may be the same image as another. A couple may show her hating it, but none may whine, plead or sneer at the player.

## Format

Plain text, no markdown, no preamble, no explanation. Exactly this shape, one line each:

A1: <line>
A2: <line>
A3: <line>
B1: <line>
B2: <line>
...
B8: <line>
result:
A1: Ireena steps back from the fray, her hand still on her pommel. Whatever comes for your throat parts around her like dark water round a stone.
A2: Ireena takes her place behind you, spine straight and blade sheathed. Nothing in this valley raises a hand to her, as if it has been warned whose she is.
A3: You draw steel while Ireena stands three paces clear, untouched and unlooked-at. Even the hungry things of the mist step wide of her shadow.
B1: Ireena's knuckles whiten on her sheathed hilt as she steps clear of the steel.
B2: Hungry eyes slide right past Ireena to fix on you alone.
B3: Ireena stands three paces behind your shoulder, her jaw set hard.
B4: Ireena swallows the sharp word on her tongue and yields the ground to you.
B5: The violence parts around Ireena's stillness as if she stood behind glass.
B6: Ireena folds her arms over her cloak, watching every blow she cannot answer.
B7: Not one blade angles toward Ireena where she waits at the roadside.
B8: Ireena measures the distance between your back and the dark with level eyes.
